When a tag has no GPS fix, the app estimates the area from the repeaters the tag heard. The list comes from the public MeshCore map (about 60 MB to download, better on Wi-Fi).
The whole list is downloaded and searched on this phone. Your tags\' positions never leave the phone for this.
The app reminds you to update it after 30 days.
A GPS tag on the MeshCore mesh. Reports are sealed with a ratcheting key and only this phone can read them. No account and no server of ours in the middle.
When the tag has no GPS fix, the app shows an area estimated from the repeaters it heard, with how sure that is. It never shows a guess as a point.

Updating over USB from the phone comes later. Until then, update from a computer.

1. Connect the tag to a computer with a USB-C cable.
2. Double-press the reset button: a drive appears.
3. Copy the LibreTag firmware %1$s (.uf2) onto the drive. The tag restarts by itself.
4. Plug it back into this phone: the pairing stays, the app unlocks it as before.

While it scans here, the tag briefly announces itself over Bluetooth so nearby devices answer with their names.
The tag can scan Bluetooth on the spot and send what it saw with its next report. Useful in Lost mode: it shows which devices are around it.

Pairing only lets the tag recognise a phone nearby, so it knows its owner is close. It gives that phone no access to the tag and sends nothing anywhere. A phone changes its Bluetooth address every few minutes, and pairing once lets the tag recognise it anyway.\n\nFor 2 minutes the tag shows up as \"LibreTag\". Pair with it in the Bluetooth settings of the phone it should know: this one or another, for example your second phone. Repeat for each phone.

resources.string: kept by the tag while quiet, never sent (USB)
Checks and parked quiet need firmware 0.7 or newer.
Not set up. Without a backup, a lost phone means re-pairing every tag over the cable.
The backup keeps your tags\' keys encrypted on Nostr relays, so you can restore your tags on a new phone or open them in the web version. This phone updates both copies below after every change.
Sign in with your Nostr signer (Amber, or a bunker on another device). The copy is encrypted to your npub, and only your signer can open it.
The copy for your npub stays on the relays and you can sign in again later. You can also delete it from the relays now.
LibreTag makes 12 words for you. They restore your tags even when the phone with your signer is gone. Write them on paper.
This phone keeps the copy up to date. The phrase itself isn\'t stored here.
The relays that answer remove this copy. A relay or anyone who copied it earlier may still keep it, but without the phrase it can\'t be opened.
Waiting for your signer. Tap Save now to approve it.
No relay answered. It will try again after the next change.
The copy on the relays was made by a newer version and this one can\'t read it.
This copy was deleted from another device. Create it again if you want it back.
Version 0.7.0 saved a backup with a passphrase you chose. This version uses a recovery phrase instead. Create one, then delete the old backup.
The backup holds each tag\'s pairing key. Whoever opens it can read the tag\'s whole history and send it commands.
LibreTag asks your signer to encrypt the backup to your npub and to sign it. The signer asks you once whether to allow that.
No signer app on this phone. Install Amber, or use a signer on another device below.
Scan this code with your signer, or open the link in a signer on this phone.
This code has expired. Make a new one.
That isn\'t a bunker:// link with a relay.
Signed in. Looking for your backup…
Signed in. The backup for your npub is saved.
Write these 12 words on paper, in this order. Anyone who has them can open your backup. LibreTag doesn\'t keep them and can\'t show them again.
Type words 3, 7 and 11 from your paper.
That doesn\'t match. Look at your paper again.
If you already keep a Bitcoin seed safe, you can use a BIP-85 child phrase from your wallet instead. Choose Restore with phrase and type it there.
Recovery phrase set. The backup is saved.
Never type your wallet\'s seed here. Use the phrase LibreTag made, or a BIP-85 child phrase from your wallet.
Not a word from the list: %1$s
The words don\'t fit together. Check each one against your paper.
Looking for the backup on the relays…
You can start a new backup with this phrase, for example a BIP-85 child phrase from your wallet.
No relay answered. Check your connection.
Found the backup. All its tags are already on this phone.
